messages:
sophia: quick heads-up — I'm about to open a small terraform change for the k-provisioner that: allows limited spot fallback, tweaks drain behavior, and increases HPA maxReplicas for a hot path. Really want a quick safety check before PR. diff inline.

sophia: TL;DR: add `spotFallback.enabled = true`, `spotFallback.percent = 20`, set `ttlSecondsUntilExpired = 300` for provisioner, and add preStop hook sleep on the node bootstrap to reduce simultaneous cold starts. HPA maxReplicas bumped 50->70 for frontend-route.

sophia: terraform snippet:
```hcl
resource "karpenter_provisioner" "compute" {
  name = "compute-prod"
  requirements = ["node.kubernetes.io/instance-type =~ t3.* || m5.*"]
  taint { key = "spot-fallback"; effect = "NoSchedule" }
  ttl_seconds_until_expired = 300
  spot_fallback {
    enabled = true
    percent = 20
  }
}
```

kevin: quick Q — is the HPA target using CPU requests or custom metrics? we should avoid raising maxReplicas if metrics are based on pod CPU requests that are underprovisioned.

sophia: HPA is currently CPU (targetUtilization 60) for frontend-route; the bump is because request spikes hit queue and we get tail latency. Idea is to allow more concurrent pods during burst windows.

kevin: if it's targetUtilization=60 that's fine but please keep an eye on burst costs. also consider 2-step rollout: first raise to 60 then to 70 after 24h soak. :thinking_face:

ana: small flag: the bootstrap change adds a new secret key path for node-kubeconfig at `secrets/kube/bootstrap:v2`. ops will need to rotate the vault mount in the cluster bootstrap job.

ana: command to update prod secret (ops-runbook):
```bash
kubectl -n infra create secret generic node-bootstrap --from-file=kubeconfig=./kubeconfig_v2 --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -
```

mike: are we doing this as single-cluster change? can we mark a small subset of provisioners for canary to avoid cluster-wide churn? we should also temporarily add annotation to pods to opt-out of node draining during the canary window.

mike: example annot to skip drain: `kubectl annotate node <name> karpenter.sh/drain-skip=true` — not ideal but ok for a short canary.

sophia: good call. I'll add a `canary = true` flag to a new provisioner resource and keep the existing provisioner untouched for now. will include drain-skip annotation docs in the PR.

deploy-bot: [automation] CI: queued terraform fmt + plan for pr/infra/1867501234 (expected ~3m).

kevin: also add a note in the README about fallback percent rationale and how to revert quickly. we had a spot-fallback incident last year — prefer smaller increments. :thumbsup:

sophia: will do. I'll open the PR with the canary provisioner, bootstrap secret notes, and a short smoke test checklist. tagging you all in the PR for review. thanks!

kevin: acked, will review once CI passes. :thumbsup:
